sections.h2: Who bills and assesses property tax in Old Bridge?
sections.html:
Old Bridge Township has its own Tax Assessor and its own Tax Collection office, and both work out of the township's government offices. The assessor values each parcel. The collector bills and takes payment at (732) 721-5600, extension 2999. The township belongs to Middlesex County, so value disputes are heard in New Brunswick.

The township runs an online account system where owners can view current-year and prior-year tax details, confirm that a payment arrived, and pay by bank account or card. Nominal fees apply to online payments. To view a balance, create a login with the Web Login ID printed on the latest bill. An owner who cannot find the bill can email the collection office to get the ID. Weekday collector hours run 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., and the office has added Saturday sessions from 9 a.m. to 1 p.m. around a due date, so call to ask about the next one.

Old Bridge covers 38.18 square miles of land in the Raritan Valley, faces Staten Island across Raritan Bay and sits roughly 25 miles from New York City. The 2020 count was 66,876 people, and the 2025 estimate of 70,228 is a 5.0% rise. There is no single downtown. The township is a set of communities: Laurence Harbor, Madison Park, Brownville, Parlin, Cheesequake and the Old Bridge center, with ZIP codes 08857, 08859, 08879 and 07735.

For 2020 to 2024, 70.4% of homes were owner-occupied, a typical home was valued at $461,000 and a typical household earned $104,587. The mean commute is 36.1 minutes. Routes 9, 18, 34 and 35 cross the township, and the Garden State Parkway passes through with Interchange 120 signed for Laurence Harbor and Matawan, so buyers who commute will look at how close a house sits to those roads.

State law sets four installments, each mailed ahead of its due date. A grace period of ten days is optional and set by township resolution, and the ceiling on late interest is 8% a year up to $1,500 and 18% above.

A bill that goes out late must give at least 25 days to pay, and interest then runs from the original due date. Old Bridge's fourth quarter bills in 2025 drew a township statement, because the third quarter had been estimated on a 4.79% rise while the final 2025 increase came in near 10%.

sections.h2: Why did Old Bridge tax bills jump in 2025?
sections.html:
School tax makes up about 60% of the total property tax bill. The school levy rose 13.87% in 2025, while the municipal tax rate rose 1.58%. The final 2025 and preliminary 2026 bill went out in late August or early September, and owners with questions about the school budget are sent to the Board of Education at 732-566-1000.

A third quarter estimate can understate the year, and the fourth quarter then carries the catch-up. Before choosing a closing date, pull the full year's billed and paid amounts from the collector, and have the closing agent prorate against the actual bill rather than the estimate.

sections.h2: How to appeal an Old Bridge assessment
sections.html:
Owners file with the Middlesex County Board of Taxation, 75 Bayard Street, 4th Floor, New Brunswick, phone 732-745-3350. Petitions can be filed online through an account. Evidence may go up with the petition or as late as seven calendar days before the hearing, by 4:00 p.m., and the system routes the petition to the board, the assessor and the clerk. The board does not hold virtual hearings. Its office, which serves twenty-five municipalities, is open Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 4:15 p.m.

  • A regular petition has an April 1 cutoff, moved to May 1 if the township revalued or reassessed.
  • Added and omitted assessment appeals are due December 1, and the county must receive them, not just see a postmark.
  • You must be current on taxes through the first quarter of the tax year to proceed.
  • Appeals cover value only, never the tax rate set by the budgets.

Owners unhappy with the board's judgment have 45 days from mailing to go to the state Tax Court, and an assessment over $1,000,000 may start there.

sections.h2: Relief programs for Old Bridge owners
sections.html:
The state's ANCHOR program gives property tax relief to New Jersey owners and renters who live in the property as a main home and meet income limits. One combined form covers Senior Freeze, ANCHOR and Stay NJ. Ask the state for the current filing window.

About 17.8% of residents are 65 or older, so many owners may qualify for something.

  • Senior Freeze reimburses increases in tax on a main home.
  • ANCHOR covers owners and renters under the income limits.
  • Local deductions for qualifying veteran, senior and disabled owners come from the township assessor.

A seller who receives any of these should ask the assessor what happens to the deduction once the house is sold, so there are no surprises on the next bill.

sections.h2: What should an Old Bridge seller check before listing?
sections.html:
The township has a Rent Stabilization Board, a Building and Code department and a Zoning Board, so landlords and anyone with an unfinished project should check each office before a sale. Ask the building department whether permits for a deck, basement or addition are closed, and ask the assessor whether an added assessment is pending.

Deed filing happens at the Middlesex County Clerk, whose office can give the current fee schedule. The collector can issue a payoff letter good through the closing date. All of Old Bridge Township lies within the Old Bridge school district, so school boundaries are the same across the township.

The order of work is simple. Get the payoff letter, close out any open permits, confirm whether an appeal is pending, and then set the closing date. A cash buyer buying as-is will still ask for the payoff and the permit history, but skips repair requests and a lender's appraisal, which usually shortens the timeline.

faqs.q: Who do I call about Old Bridge property tax?
faqs.a: Call the Tax Collector's office at (732) 721-5600, extension 2999. It bills and collects the tax, and the Tax Assessor handles valuation.

faqs.q: Where do Old Bridge assessment appeals go?
faqs.a: They go to the Middlesex County Board of Taxation in New Brunswick, which takes petitions through an online portal. April 1 is the regular cutoff, and May 1 follows a revaluation.

faqs.q: What share of an Old Bridge tax bill is school tax?
faqs.a: About 60% in 2025. That year the school levy rose 13.87% and the municipal rate rose 1.58%.

faqs.q: Can I pay Old Bridge property tax online?
faqs.a: Yes. The township's online system accepts payments from a bank account or card, and nominal processing fees apply. Owners need a web login ID, which is printed on the tax bill.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Old Bridge house with tax owing?
faqs.a: Yes. The closing agent pays the collector out of the seller's proceeds, using a written payoff figure that is good for the closing date.
